title: Update Private upgrade docs: new installer commands, troubleshooting, rollback guidance
author: Elliot Price
description: Summary: Align Private (VPC + on-prem/air-gapped) upgrade/rollback documentation with the new installer workflow: plan -> prechecks -> backup -> apply -> verify -> rollback (if needed). This updates the operator-facing steps, introduces troubleshooting playbooks for common precheck and upgrade failures, and clarifies rollback guarantees/limitations (esp. around schema migrations and partial rollouts). Motivation: Support escalations and design partner feedback indicated the previous docs were ambiguous about (a) which checks are blocking vs warning, (b) what gets backed up and how to validate restore readiness, and (c) when rollback is safe vs when manual intervention is required. This PR is the docs companion to private-installer changes (upgrade plan generator, preflight framework, backup orchestrator, rollback state machine) and Helm ordering changes (control plane before data plane). Audience/visibility: Internal runbooks + external-ish docs pages that are shared with Private customers under guidance. What changed (high level): 1) Rewrote the main upgrade procedure to use new commands and phase naming: Generate plan, Run prechecks, Create backup, Apply upgrade (control plane then data plane), Post-upgrade verification, Capture artifacts/support bundle. 2) Added a troubleshooting index for: precheck failures (storage headroom, DB connectivity, OIDC reachability, TLS/DNS), migration lock timeouts, stuck Helm hooks/jobs, artifact/bundle verification errors for air-gapped upgrades, and rollback failures. 3) Added explicit rollback guidance: rollback entry points, expected time, health checks, and a decision tree for 'rollback vs fix-forward' based on stage. 4) Updated on-prem/air-gapped section with offline bundle verification expectations (checksums/signatures), mirror endpoints, and common operator mistakes. 5) Added an 'Upgrade artifacts for auditability' section describing what the installer persists (plan JSON, precheck results, backup IDs, execution log, audit events) and what to attach to support tickets. Notes: This PR intentionally does not introduce net-new policy; it documents the gating/checklist already being formalized elsewhere. Where behavior is still being finalized, wording is 'as of Private installer >= 1.9.0' and points to release notes. Checklist: - [x] Steps match installer CLI (plan/apply/rollback) - [x] Troubleshooting covers top 5 support cases (SUP-18421, SUP-18488, SUP-18510, SUP-18577) - [x] On-prem/air-gapped guidance includes bundle verification and offline registries - [x] Security reviewed language around backups/secrets (no plaintext exports, KMS/HSM expectations) - [x] Link check + docs build + Vale pass

notable_snippets: Installer command flow (excerpt): redwood-private upgrade plan --target 1.12.0 --output /var/lib/redwood/upgrade/plan.json ; redwood-private upgrade precheck run --plan /var/lib/redwood/upgrade/plan.json ; redwood-private upgrade backup create --plan /var/lib/redwood/upgrade/plan.json ; redwood-private upgrade apply --plan /var/lib/redwood/upgrade/plan.json ; redwood-private upgrade verify --plan /var/lib/redwood/upgrade/plan.json

Rollback decision point (excerpt): If failure occurs before control-plane migrations complete, prefer rollback. If failure occurs after irreversible schema migration (plan marks step as non-reversible), stop and contact Redwood Support for manual intervention steps; do not repeatedly toggle apply/rollback.

Also add a sentence about upgrade windows and release gating. Elliot Price: Added a dedicated 'Migration lock timeout' page with safe mitigations and a 'do not' list.
